I'd like the contact form that sends an email from a webpage using php to collect the IP address of the sender. The only reason is that I'd like to have a visual clue that if I (or another recipient) receives a lot of emails, they are (or are not) coming from the same person. I'm not asking this for a major enterprise solution, but in my experience crawlers that find targets for code injection don't care how big a company is.

Anyway, here's the solution I threw together rq.

$ip = clean($_SERVER["REMOTE_ADDR"]); //trims, strips slashes and special chars
$body = "Sent from".$ip."/r/n".$body;

Do any of you see a glaring problem with this? From research it appears that "REMOTE_ADDR" may not be the most reliable thing to use for an accurate client IP, but I'm not too worried about that. I'm more worried that malicious code could be injected through some way I'm not thinking of.
collecting IPs from contact pages for a small site

Remember that $_SERVER is set by your webserver, not by clients.

In the case of REMOTE_ADDR, there's not really room for a client to inject anything.

The IPs in emails have so far matched what I get from whatismyip.com. To clarify for my understanding, $_SERVER provides the IP it gathers when the page is accessed, correct? That is, once a client connects, the IP that the server is sending information to is the same as what I get from $_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR']. Or am I mistaken?. ...

While not impossible, $_SERVER['REMOTE_ADDR'] is alot more difficult to spoof than a good majority of the other methods that are out there. Other methods are also prone to returning false if a user is behind a proxy.
